newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks bounce back, led by Van der Horst.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks bounce back, led by Van der Horst.

text.p: Singapore shares were stirred from the doldrums late on Tuesday, helped by a revival in demand for beleaguered Van der Horst, dealers said.

"The market was thin but topical in one stock...there was some serious accumulation going on in the last half hour of trade," a dealer with a foreign brokerage said. He noted some bargain-hunting after officials of engineering-based Van der Horst met analysts at midday to assure them the company was sound, and said momentum intensified toward the market close.
The Straits Times Industrials Index closed up 6.59 points at 2,041.38, with turnover a light 159 million shares.
Dealers said the pick-up in Vander Horst was encouraging and could signal a return of confidence for the week despite a dramatic drop in Wall Street on Monday.
"The Dow Jones was certainly no incentive but the market is more focused on (local company) results," a bank dealer said.

Small-capitalised stocks like Heshe Holdings saw 41 million shares crossed at Singapore 30 cents each. The share ended up two cents at 35 cents. Raffles Medical, Informatics and Excel Machine all hit new year highs in active trade.
Van der Horst ended eight cents higher at S$2.27, after skidding to a new low of S$1.98.
